question: Which of the following best explains why phenol reacts with aqueous NaOH but alcohol does not?
optionA: Phenol has a lower boiling point than alcohol.
optionB: Alcohols contain a strong O-H bond that cannot be broken by weak bases.
optionC: Phenol form hydrogen bonding that facilitates ionization.
optionD: Phenol is weakly acidic due to resonance stabilization of phenoxide ion.
explanation: When phenol loses a proton (H+), the resulting phenoxide ion is stabilized by resonance (the negative charge delocalizes into the benzene ring). This makes phenol acidic enough to react with NaOH. Alcohols lack this resonance stabilization.
explanationA: Incorrect. Boiling point doesn't determine acidity.
explanationB: Incorrect. The O-H bond in phenol is actually weaker due to resonance.
explanationC: Incorrect. H-bonding doesn't facilitate ionization to a base.
explanationD: Correct! Resonance stabilization of phenoxide makes phenol acidic.
